html:
SMTO-LLM-0076 — SMTO couldn't switch to the local model with the current setup

GUID: e4e68fe0-7ec9-5795-adb0-b0fff74876c2
Slug: local-ai-activation-failed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't safely point its Main model at this model server. Either the server's API key differs from the key Main uses, or SMTO has no address it can reach the server at. Your current Main model hasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, and on the Main card check whether an API key is saved or Use no API key is on. SMTO won't send Main's key to a new server, or a new key to Main, so the two must already match.
  2. Open Parameter Store and make the Local AI API key entry linked to your profile match Main's key, or remove the link if neither uses a key. Matching keys let SMTO switch without moving a password somewhere it wasn't meant to go.
  3. If the Gateway is on another computer, add to the Local AI Runtime profile the address SMTO's own server should use to reach the model server (the setting named in Technical details). The Gateway's own local address only works on that computer, not from SMTO's server.
  4. Ask SMTO to preview switching to your local model again, using the updated profile. The preview re-checks the key and address before anything changes.

What success looks like

  • The preview succeeds, and after applying it the Main card in Settings › Setup › Model routing shows your local model.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste Main's API key into chat messages to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Local AI activation was refused because the profile's API key does not match the Main credential, a remote Gateway's profile lacks a controller-reachable URL, or a read-side service failure occurred during activation.

What this means

  • Activation cannot safely reuse the selected credential or establish a controller-reachable route; read-side service failures can also reach this fallback. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • Activation cannot safely reuse the selected credential or establish a controller-reachable route; read-side service failures can also reach this fallback.

How to diagnose it

  • Check accepted credential selection and controller reachability separately; a remote Gateway's loopback address is not the controller's loopback.

How to fix it

  • Make the profile's api_key_ref secret equal the Main credential in Settings › Setup › Model routing (or use no key on both), and for a non-loopback Gateway set controller_base_url in the Local AI Runtime profile to a URL the Server can reach (for example an SSH tunnel). Accept the updated Parameters for the task, then create a fresh activation_preview. If the key and URL already agree, the error came from a read-side OSError/RuntimeError fallback in the Local AI service; check the Server log at the failure time.
  • Correct the explicit controller-reachable URL and accepted credential configuration, then regenerate the preview.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • Activation preview verifies the intended controller route and accepted credential without repurposing a secret.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
